title: 194-year-old tortoise has exceptional DNA repair systems that fight off ageing | New Scientist
description: The genome of Jonathan the giant tortoise, a 194-year-old resident of St Helena island, has been probed to understand how he has been alive for more than double his species’ average life expectancy
author: James Woodford

title: Neanderthal Europe was as much a wooden age as a stone age | New Scientist
description: When Neanderthals dominated Europe, it was likely that wood was at least as important to them as stone for working into tools
author: James Woodford

title: Why gatekeeping is needed in the age of AI | New Scientist
description: Large language models have unleashed a torrent of text – dealing with it won't be easy
author: New Scientist

title: Colonisation of Australia led to big increase in wildfire danger | New Scientist
description: An analysis of lake sediments in south-eastern Australia has revealed that the expulsion of Indigenous communities in the 19th century resulted in an explosion of tree cover and more devastating wildfires
author: James Woodford

title: Stunning early mammal fossil sheds light on the evolution of suckling | New Scientist
description: A predecessor of modern mammals that lived in the Jurassic has been found in China with its throat anatomy preserved, allowing researchers to examine the earliest evidence for the evolution of suckling
author: James Woodford

title: OpenAI announces 722 mathematical discoveries in one go | New Scientist
description: AI has been growing ever more capable in mathematics and OpenAI has now released hundreds of papers at the same time – to the astonishment of mathematicians
author: Matthew Sparkes
